P1.evidence: Standard opener: 'I've seen your application that you sent to us, but I would like to get in more depth on what's actually been going on and what have you tried and how can we actually help you?' The application is referenced but not read back. Notably this single question folds in the P4 opener as well, which is why past attempts land early and well. No four-part frame, and no explicit agreement sought beyond a trailing 'Cool.' The cost shows up at the end: the prospect had no idea payment was expected today and asked to be sent a link instead.

P2.evidence: Five clean hits, the strongest baseline in the batch. Work: 'on a daily basis, you're mostly sitting, or how does it look like in your work?' Injuries asked directly — 'do you have any injuries from the past that are occurring right now?' — and then pursued anatomically with 'How about your hips?' and 'And lower back?', which produced the most useful material in the call. Training week asked and quantified: 'you mentioned that you're going five to six times a week to the gym?' Results from current training asked with genuine challenge: 'working out for four years and not seeing, like, significant results, like, four years, that's a really long period.' Diet asked twice, first generally then as a day walkthrough. Age (31) and weight (160 lb) were volunteered unprompted and height was never captured at all, so P2a misses. Health conditions were never asked — testosterone levels and a suspected gluten intolerance came from the prospect. Sleep and daytime energy were both skipped, despite the prospect volunteering 'being super exhausted' as the main thing that beats a workout, which was the obvious opening.

P3.evidence: The surface layer ran properly. Aesthetics asked outright — 'Is there like a tangible goal that you can pinpoint? Meaning maybe some aesthetics kind of thing?' — producing the slim waist, broader frame and 175-180 lb target. The can't-do question also ran: 'Do you feel you're missing out on something right now because of that?', answered 'No, but... I don't love that I can't touch my toes.' Then the phase stops dead. The bridge question was never asked, so the call never left the physical. Nobody asked what moving better would actually do for him, and nobody asked who else it impacts — this prospect's family status is entirely unknown at the end of a 45-minute call. Ageing surfaced only because he raised it himself ('as I get older, these things will only become harder and worse'), and the rep let it pass without driving it. The reflect-back was good but aimed at the surface: the gym-strong-but-can't-chop-wood analogy, which the prospect confirmed with 'That captures what I'm talking about here.' Confirming the symptom, not the why.

P4.evidence: The best-run phase on the call. What he tried and what happened were both asked, the second with real challenge about four years of limited return. The blocker question ran in its most useful form — 'What usually competes with a workout?' — drawing working late, exhaustion and better weekend offers. And the prospect named the gap himself, repeatedly and precisely: 'it's really easy for me to skip a workout', 'I'm actually the inconsistent one because I travel a lot', 'I jumped to strength training without having the flexibility and mobility part figured out', and the defeatist loop 'what's one workout even gonna do for me?' The rep reinforced it well with 'one becomes two, two becomes three, then it's a week, then it's two weeks.' What never ran was the closing move — 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' — which is the one that converts a named gap into felt need, and P4c was answered by the prospect rather than asked by the rep.

P5.evidence: Never run. No two-year projection, no settle question, no 'why not', no line in the sand. The prospect handed the rep the entry point unprompted — 'I know that as I get older, these things will only become harder and worse... when I'm much older, I'm not struggling on a day-to-day basis with feeling like I'm stiff and can't do anything' — which is a self-authored consequence frame that only needed drawing out. The rep acknowledged it and moved on. The urgency work he did do later was the OD travel play, which handles a timing objection but does not make the cost of inaction real.

P6.evidence: A belief check ran in soft, self-truncated form — 'So how do you feel overall about it on a scale from 1 to' — answered 'I think I'm excited to give it a try... so far I think I believe in what you're saying. So yeah, I feel good.' That is enthusiasm, not the scripted belief question, and it contains three hedged 'I thinks'. The all-in question never ran at all, which is the specific omission that cost this call: 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' would have surfaced the finance review before the price was on the table rather than after it. The rep moved to price on a soft yes and then met exactly the hesitation the question is designed to pre-empt.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted so the phase applies, and none of it completed. No payment collected and no link sent, despite the prospect twice asking for one — 'you can just send me the link and I'll probably pay by this weekend' and 'if there's a link to pay, then I can just pay online.' The rep declined both times on procedural grounds: 'I need to be on a call with you, because we need to have, like, we have a procedure that I get you onboarded, get you in the community.' No Trevor onboarding call was booked — the slot taken was a second call with the rep himself. No agreement, no welcome email, no Skool, no onboarding form. The only artefact that reached the prospect was a calendar invite, which landed in his spam folder.

objection_plays.detail: The best-executed play in the batch. Trigger was explicit — travel through late August and the first week of September, with 'in September when I'm back is really when I'm going to be like 100% serious.' The rep ran the spine of OD in order: tested whether the obstacle was terminal ('is this going to be the last travel that you're having?'), delivered the things-never-slow-down move with concrete examples ('you're going to get busy, no matter what... You're going to be finishing a project, mid-September, beginning of October, whatever. Christmas happens, like, there's always something'), and then isolated the real commitment with 'what does it mean I'm being 100% in, only from September, not sooner?' It worked cleanly: the prospect moved to 'if we can go ahead and get started... even as early as next week, I'll be fine.' Three of the six scripted moves did not run — the compounding-cost line, the 'what if all you had to do was show up' reframe, and the only-thing-you-can-control close — but the play achieved its purpose and the objection did not return.

Two distinct doubts were raised. On the category — 'I've never done an online coach before... there's so many online scammers' — the rep answered with an off-script exposure argument: 'if this was a scam and Trevor has been for six years now working with over a thousand clients... he would be smeared all over internet right now.' It landed, and the prospect reinforced it himself with the follower count, so the trigger resolved without any OE move being used. The second doubt was left entirely alone: 'I am a little skeptical at like how the video filming and the communication and all that stuff's going to work.' That is a mechanics doubt with an easy answer — show him the app, show him a feedback video — and the rep never returned to it. None of the scripted OE moves ran: no certainty question, no pleasure-versus-pain, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before, no 'how will you know if you never try'.

Trigger landed clearly at the close — 'I'm gonna have to look at kind of my finances and see what I can plan out.' No part of the play ran. No isolation, no should-versus-how frame, and nothing at all from the financial picture: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no available credit, no investments. The rep restated the three payment structures the prospect already had and then jumped to a holding deposit. This was an unusually soft trigger from a buyer who had just said 'that number is fine by me' and 'I pay my personal trainer far more than that' — a single isolation question would very likely have revealed there was no real financial obstacle and closed the call.

SCRIPT GAP, and the one that decided this call. The prospect asked twice to be sent a payment link and complete the purchase in his own time, and the rep refused both times on procedural grounds. There is no scripted handling for a buyer who wants to transact asynchronously, so the rep defended the process instead of the sale. The identical refusal appears in the Pukar Patel call on the same day, and in both cases a ready buyer left without paying. This is a policy question for the principal rather than a coaching note: if the onboarding sequence genuinely requires a live call, the payment step should still be separable from it.

SCRIPT GAP — imminent surgery. The prospect disclosed laser eye surgery scheduled for the following day, with a doctor's restriction already in force, while agreeing to begin loaded kettlebell training the week after. There is no scripted move requiring medical clearance before a start date, so the disclosure was treated purely as a scheduling constraint and the rep simply moved the meeting to Monday. The same absence produced a far more serious exposure in the Steve Dawson call. A clearance gate belongs in P2d.

notes: The best discovery and the best objection play in the batch attached to the worst close. P4 ran properly, OD was textbook, and the prospect finished the call pre-sold, price-accepting and naming the plan he wanted — then left without a link because the rep would not sell asynchronously. Two coachable items: ask the all-in question in P6 so a finance review surfaces before the price rather than after it, and take the payment when the buyer asks to pay. The travel objection was handled so well that it is worth using as a training clip.
